dependencies: core Lean 4 only (no mathlib, no Batteries, no external imports)
axiom_policy: Every declaration listed in `theorems` must appear in the `#print axioms` output of the pinned kernel run. Its reported axiom set must be a subset of `permitted_axioms` (the three core Lean assumptions). Any other axiom, and in particular `sorryAx`, fails the gate. The gate parses the kernel's printed output; it does not grep source comments.
frozen_graph_assumption: All theorems in the graph sections assume a simple graph in which every edge NOT incident to the single edited vertex is frozen: unchanged in presence and endpoints across the edit. Row lists are assumed to enumerate each old vertex exactly once with its pre-edit degree. Lean does not prove that the runtime constructs such a list; that is a runtime obligation.

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.stable_on
theorems.statement: radius < margin and -radius <= delta implies 0 < margin + delta (Int)
theorems.runtime_predicate: score > 0 (bit on) stays true when the integer margin strictly exceeds the integer perturbation radius

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.stable_off
theorems.statement: margin <= -radius and delta <= radius implies margin + delta <= 0 (Int)
theorems.runtime_predicate: score > 0 (bit on) stays false; equality at 0 is deliberately permitted because the runtime test is strict

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.crossing_on_iff
theorems.runtime_predicate: exact crossing boundary for the on-side; no numerical error term is modelled

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.crossing_off_iff
theorems.runtime_predicate: exact crossing boundary for the off-side, equality included

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.old_vertex_after_add
theorems.statement: iso (degree + edgeNat edge) = iso degree - hit degree edge
theorems.runtime_counterpart: per-old-vertex isolation update during an ADD
theorems.runtime_predicate: a vertex is isolated iff its integer degree is 0; only a previously isolated vertex that the new vertex attaches to can lose isolation

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.after_old_count
theorems.statement: afterOldIso rows = oldIso rows - hitIso rows
theorems.runtime_predicate: summed over every old vertex exactly once

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.add_isolation_delta
theorems.statement: (afterOldIso rows + iso (newDegree rows)) - oldIso rows = iso (newDegree rows) - hitIso rows
theorems.runtime_counterpart: exact ADD isolated-vertex ledger emitted by the point-map neighbour diagnostic
theorems.runtime_predicate: delta(isolated count) = new vertex isolated indicator - count of old isolated vertices it attached to

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.chg_hit_eval
theorems.statement: chgHit rest before after = (if rest = 0 then before-indicator - after-indicator else 0)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: per-neighbour isolation update during a CHANGE
theorems.runtime_predicate: only a neighbour whose frozen (non-incident) degree is 0 can change isolation state, and only via the toggled edge

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.change_neighbour_ledger
theorems.statement: afterIsoC rows - oldIsoC rows = chgLedger rows
theorems.runtime_predicate: summed over every other old vertex exactly once, frozen edges excluded from `rest`

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.change_isolation_delta
theorems.statement: (afterIsoC rows + iso (degAfterOf rows)) - (oldIsoC rows + iso (degBeforeOf rows)) = chgLedger rows + (iso (degAfterOf rows) - iso (degBeforeOf rows))
theorems.runtime_counterpart: exact CHANGE isolated-vertex ledger emitted by the point-map neighbour diagnostic
theorems.runtime_predicate: delta(isolated count) = neighbour ledger + the changed vertex's own isolation-indicator change; the changed vertex's degrees are recomputed from the same rows, not supplied independently

theorems.name: WayfinderBounds.change_neutral
theorems.statement: if every row has before = after then chgLedger rows = 0
theorems.runtime_counterpart: neutral CHANGE / neutral ADD regression case
theorems.runtime_predicate: an edit that toggles no incident edge must report a zero isolation ledger

runtime_verified_not_lean_proved.detail: That tools/point-map enumerates each old vertex exactly once, with the correct pre-edit degree, and with `rest` excluding edges incident to the edited vertex. Checked by runtime tests, not by the kernel.
That the runtime graph is simple and that all non-incident edges are unchanged across the edit. Assumed, not proved.

That the runtime score/threshold arithmetic is exact-integer and that its perturbation radius is a genuine bound. Any floating-point score must be reduced to exact integers before these theorems apply.

nonclaims: No fluid, velocity, pressure, or vorticity equation is proved, imported, or implied.
No Navier-Stokes / Euler result is claimed; openai/NavierStokesAndEuler is not imported and no Millennium claim is made.
No floating-point error bound is proved; all statements are exact integer arithmetic.
No probabilistic certificate, confidence interval, or calibration claim is proved.
No claim about prediction accuracy, pre-edit forecasting skill, ranking quality, or semantic task grading.
A checked ledger identity is not evidence that the runtime ledger is correctly wired; see runtime_verified_not_lean_proved.
Retrospective replay agreement on stored maps is not a forecasting result.
No keep/revert, deletion, or ranking rule is justified by these theorems.

statement_pinning.pin: sha256 of the normalized Lean statement text
statement_pinning.normalization: Lean comments stripped (/- -/ nested blocks, -- line); string literals respected; statement = source text between the declaration name and the first top-level ':=' (or the first top-level match-arm '|' line for pattern proofs); whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces; proof text excluded.
statement_pinning.policy: A pin mismatch fails CI. A legitimate statement change requires a deliberate pin regeneration in the same PR, with the statement diff reviewed as a semantic change. Do NOT regenerate pins to make CI pass without reviewing the statement diff.

definitions.pin: sha256 over the sorted 'command-key:normalized-text' entries of EVERY top-level command in the lean_file -- imports, open/namespace/end wrappers, attribute lines (hashed WITH the declaration they decorate), declarations of any kind, set_option lines, #print/#eval/#check, notation/syntax/macro/elab, run_cmd blocks (comments stripped, whitespace collapsed). theorem/lemma/example proof bodies are EXCLUDED: the hashed text is the statement through the first top-level ':=' (inclusive) or up to the first match-arm line. 'decls' maps each command key (<kind>:<name>, or <kind> with #N collision suffixes for unnamed commands) to its own normalized-text sha256
definitions.policy: A commands-hash mismatch FAILS CI even when every theorem statement is unchanged: adding ANY top-level command (including an attribute-prefixed declaration, which round 2's line-start keyword regex missed), redefining a definition, or adding a set_option/#print/notation line changes what the pinned theorems actually prove or how the file elaborates, so a legitimate change requires a deliberate definitions-block regeneration IN THE SAME PR, with the command diff reviewed as a semantic change. Do NOT regenerate the block to make CI pass without reviewing the diff. Proof-body-only rewrites (kernel-checked content) do NOT change the hash and need no regeneration. A block pinning zero commands is refused (vacuous pin), and a block whose schema is not commands-v2 FAILS the gate (fail-closed; an old definition-pins/1 defs-only block cannot be verified against command hashing).
